mitigation_descriptions: The sudoers file should be strictly edited such that passwords are always required and that users can’t spawn risky processes as users with higher privilege. By requiring a password, even if an adversary can get terminal access, they must know the password to run anything in the sudoers file.

Setting the timestamp_timeout to 0 will require the user to input their password every time sudo is executed. Similarly, ensuring that the tty_tickets setting is enabled will prevent this leakage across tty sessions.
Prevent adversary access to privileged accounts or access necessary to perform this technique. Consider removing and replacing system components suspected of being compromised.
reasoning: The investigator confirmed that an unauthorized account transition from www-data to jhall occurred on intranet-server, followed by credential dumping from /etc/shadow via sudo privileges. Immediate containment is required to stop credential exposure and unauthorized administrative access.
remediation_plan: 1. Isolate the affected host intranet-server (10.143.2.4) from the network to prevent lateral movement. 2. Terminate active sessions and revoke active credentials for user account jhall and the www-data service. 3. Rotate all system credentials and passwords potentially exposed through the /etc/shadow read. 4. Strictly audit and edit the sudoers configuration to ensure passwords are required and restrict users from executing risky binaries with elevated privileges. 5. Configure timestamp_timeout to 0 and enable tty_tickets to prevent sudo privilege caching and leakage across sessions.
